title: Week of 23 September · Tell a family-life story
description: For the week of 23 September: one guided chat and one short written answer. The chat replaces the separate speaking rehearsal. A real or made-up story is fine; no deadline has been set.
objectives: Tell connected past events in a clear order and explain why something happened.
Improve two useful past verbs in your own words.
source: Original Rory’s English practice linked to English in Context 5, Unit 1: Family life (pp. 20–25); not a textbook exercise.

tasks.prompt: After Chat 1, write your best version of the story here in 5–7 sentences. A family member or friend can be in it. Use first, then and finally, at least four past events, and a reason with because. Include one question the people could ask next time to avoid the mix-up. Check two past verbs, then press Send answers to Rory. You do not need to copy the conversation transcript.

title: Week of 30 September · An email about a family weekend
description: Start from 30 September. One guided chat, one short email and a quick check. The chat replaces the separate speaking rehearsal. A fictional family is fine. This is a shorter first draft towards the book’s roughly 200-word email task; no deadline has been set.
objectives: Organise an informal email for a friend.
Use present forms for a usual routine and past verbs for a weekend event.
source: Original Rory’s English practice linked to English in Context 5, Unit 1: Family life (especially p. 25); shorter practice draft, not the textbook exercise.

tasks.prompt: After Chat 2, write a 120–150-word email to an imaginary friend about family life. Use a greeting and friendly ending. Say what your family or invented group usually does, tell a short story about last weekend in the past tense, and explain one thing you like or would change. Use because and one other linking word. Check one past-tense sentence and one usually sentence in this same box, then press Send answers to Rory. You do not need to copy the conversation transcript.
